title: Security review: audit logging + RBAC for Cost Model API reads
creator: Felix Schneider
description:
We need security sign-off and implementation guidance for audit logging + access controls for Cost Model API reads. The SCM outputs are not billing, but they are customer-sensitive (unit economics + potentially per-route attribution).

Scope:
1) Define audit events for Cost Model API reads (estimate + explain/attribution), including required fields, redaction rules, and retention.
2) RBAC: who can call these endpoints and what scope is allowed (tenant-admin vs billing role vs support).
3) Restricted visibility rules: ensure Console/Optimize only display aggregated or authorized breakdowns; define internal access policy and break-glass.

Stakeholders / reviewers:
- Security: Dr. Aisha Rahman (review), Marcus Lin (implementation review)
- Audit logging: Kevin Osei
- Console: Dylan Brooks / Chloe Martin
- Platform: Priya Natarajan / Jordan Lee

Notes:
- This work must land before we expand rollout beyond canary tenants. Console currently has a feature-flagged client and will degrade to basic/legacy cost view when SCM unavailable; RBAC failures must be explicit and not appear as '$0'.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Audit events emitted for all Cost Model API read paths (sync HTTP + internal service calls) with stable schema and tests.
2) Audit log payload contains actor + tenant + scope + endpoint + decision; explicitly excludes prompts, generated text, and any customer secret material.
3) RBAC policy documented and enforced in the gateway/service: least privilege by default; clear 403 vs 401 behavior.
4) Internal access rules defined (support + security only), including justification field and linkable ticket ID.
5) Retention + access to audit logs aligns with compliance baseline (min 365 days) and integrates with existing audit pipeline.
6) Security reviewers sign off with any follow-ups filed as separate tickets.
implementation_plan:
A) Audit event definitions
- Event names (proposed):
  - cost_model.read.estimate
  - cost_model.read.explain
  - cost_model.read.batchEstimate (if/when we add batch endpoints)
- Trigger points:
  - After authn/authz decision is made (log decision=ALLOW/DENY)
  - Before response serialization (log response metadata only; no full breakdown by default)

B) Required audit fields
- timestamp
- request_id / trace_id
- tenant_id (required)
- actor_type: user | api_key | service_account | employee
- actor_id (subject identifier)
- auth_context: roles/scopes used for decision
- endpoint: /v1/cost-model:estimate | /v1/cost-model:explain
- scm_version_requested + scm_version_resolved
- deployment_mode: hosted | dedicated | private
- resource_scope:
  - customer_scope: tenant | org | route (if route-scoped requests exist)
  - model_id (allowed)
  - region (allowed)
- decision: ALLOW | DENY
- deny_reason (if DENY): missing_scope | tenant_mismatch | restricted_field | unsupported_version | other
- client_app: console | optimize | internal_tool | unknown
- network: ip (for user/api_key), service_identity (for mTLS)

C) Redaction / data minimization
- MUST NOT log: prompt text, completions, tool arguments, raw token streams, customer-provided metadata fields that may contain PII.
- SHOULD NOT log full breakdown component numbers for per-request reads (risk: exposing proprietary unit economics + high cardinality). Instead log:
  - response_size_bytes
  - breakdown_present (true/false)
  - confidence_band: high | medium | low
  - assumptions_count
  - validation_mode: strict | degraded
- If Security wants numeric costs auditable, prefer sampled + aggregated pipeline (separate work) rather than stuffing into audit event.

D) RBAC policy (initial)
- External customer users:
  - Tenant Admin: allowed to read estimate + explain for their tenant.
  - Billing / Finance role (if present in RBAC): allowed.
  - Regular members: estimate allowed only if scoped to their own projects/routes; explain requires Billing or Admin.
- Service-to-service:
  - Console backend service account: allowed for tenant-scoped reads only; cannot request cross-tenant.
  - Optimize service account: allowed for 'what-if' estimates only when tenant has Optimize enabled; explain endpoint restricted unless explicitly needed for UX.
- Internal employee access:
  - Deny by default.
  - Allow only via support tool with scope support:cost-read + mandatory justification + ticket_id.
  - Break-glass requires security group membership and elevated logging.

E) Enforcement
- Primary enforcement in API gateway where possible (route-level scopes), with service-side secondary checks (tenant_id + actor scopes).
- Ensure 403 (forbidden) is distinct from validation errors; Console must not treat authz failures as '$0'.
comments: 2025-02-12 (Kevin Osei): +1 on logging ALLOW/DENY + version resolved. Please avoid logging the cost breakdown numbers themselves; we’ve had prior issues with sensitive financial inference. Log confidence_band + assumptions_count instead.

2025-02-13 (Chloe Martin): Console needs explain for tooltips (why cost changed) but can live with estimate-only in initial rollout if explain is restricted. Biggest risk is UI showing $0 when SCM errors; we’ll treat 401/403 as 'Not authorized' state and fall back to legacy view.

2025-02-14 (Dr. Aisha Rahman): Treat per-route cost breakdown as customer-sensitive. Internal access must be explicit (support tool) with justification + ticket id in audit logs. Ensure prompts/completions never enter audit stream. Also ensure private deployments don’t leak tenant identifiers across customer-owned logging sinks; tenant_id is fine if it’s the customer’s own tenant in their environment.
2025-02-18 (Jordan Lee): Version negotiation: please include both requested and resolved versions in the audit event. We saw clients silently falling back; security asked for traceability.

2025-02-24 (Marcus Lin): Proposed RBAC: estimate is broadly allowed for tenant members, explain restricted to tenant admins/billing. Service accounts get tenant-scoped access only. Implementing deny_reason codes to help Console UX without leaking internals.
status_updates: 2025-02-18: Drafted audit event schema + RBAC rules, circulated to Security/Audit/Console for review.
2025-02-26: Implemented audit event emission for estimate + explain (ALLOW/DENY) and added redaction guardrails (schema-level allowlist).
2025-03-03: Added gateway scope checks + service-side tenant enforcement; Console updated to handle 403 as explicit unauthorized state (no '$0').
2025-03-06: Security sign-off received (Aisha + Kevin). Remaining follow-ups tracked separately: numeric-cost sampling/aggregation for forensic analysis (future).
resolution: Merged audit event emission and RBAC enforcement for Cost Model API reads; documented restricted visibility rules for Console/Optimize; security reviewers approved for canary rollout expansion with least-privilege access.
follow_ups: File ticket: add aggregated/sampled numeric-cost telemetry for forensic debugging (separate from audit logs).
File ticket: define and implement 'billing' RBAC role mapping for tenants without Finance role today (fallback to Admin).
File ticket: add automated policy tests in CI to prevent accidental widening of internal employee access.
